title: Frame Foot Crack Repair by Blend and Bonded Angle at the Cargo Floor Beam Interface

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Interim repair of a crack at the frame foot to cargo floor beam interface, combining a blend of the corner radius with a bonded angle that carries the load around the blended area.

sections.purpose: Interim repair of a crack in the inboard corner radius of a frame foot at the cargo floor beam interface, using a blend followed by a bonded angle across the blended region.
sections.damage_assessment: The crack is found in the inboard corner radius of the foot, almost always on the left hand side and within the station range where the floor beam reaction is highest. The assessment must establish the cumulative blend depth at that foot from the structural repair record before any material is removed, because the limiting factor is the material remaining rather than the crack itself. A foot that has been blended twice has no remaining allowance and must be replaced rather than repaired. The extent of the crack must be established by eddy current with a radius head probe; a visual assessment consistently underestimates it because the crack runs into the radius. Adjacent stations must be inspected, since findings at neighbouring feet are common on high-cycle aircraft.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the cargo compartment lining and floor panels to expose the foot. Remove the protective treatment from the repair area. Establish the crack extent by eddy current using the radius head probe. Blend the corner radius to remove the crack completely, keeping within the blend depth limit and the cumulative allowance from the repair record. Confirm removal by eddy current at each blending increment. Measure and record the blended depth. Prepare the bonded surface on the foot and on the adjacent web to the surface preparation standard. Bond the angle across the blended region, positioning it as shown on repair drawing RD-53-21-11-005, and cure under the pressure and temperature schedule given. Install the mechanical fasteners through the angle into the foot at the pattern shown, using collars EN650523-18 and rivets AGS622474-67. The shear tie D5321112601390 is disturbed for access and reinstated. Restore the protective treatment over the whole repair area.
sections.inspection_requirements: Eddy current inspection of the blended radius after blending and again after the angle is bonded. Ultrasonic inspection of the bond line to confirm no disbond at the angle edges. A repeat eddy current inspection of the repaired foot is required every 3 000 flight cycles, and a repeat ultrasonic inspection of the bond line every 6 000 flight cycles. The repair is life limited to 18 000 flight cycles from embodiment, after which the foot must be replaced.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Cracks up to 18 mm in the corner radius, not extending into the foot flange, and only where the cumulative blend depth at that foot is below the stated allowance.

repair_drawings.title: Bonded angle across blended frame foot radius

materials.description: PLATE, DIFFUSION, USED AS BONDED ANGLE STOCK

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two rows, twelve fasteners each side of the blend, 18 mm pitch, 12 mm edge distance
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Repair is life limited to 18 000 flight cycles from embodiment with a repeat eddy current inspection every 3 000 cycles. It is an interim scheme and the foot must be replaced at the life limit.
